 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Domantas Sabonis will start Sunday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 The Kings will not have Keegan Murray for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. Achiuwa will fill the void, raising his fantasy ceiling in the final game of Week 1.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Keegan Murray (ankle) is now out for Sunday’s game against the Grizzles. 
 Murray was initially questionable for Sunday’s game, but will now be sidelined. Precious Achiuwa will look to benefit and likely start in place of Murray. Fantasy managers should keep an eye ahead of Week 2. 
 Keegan Murray 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #13 
 Keegan Murray (ankle) is now doubtful for Sunday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Murray, who was initially questionable for Sunday’s game, is on track to sit after the status downgrade. If he can’t play, Precious Achiuwa may benefit most, as he’s likely to replace Murray in the starting lineup. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa got 14 points (7-of-11 FGs), six rebounds, an assist and a steal on Friday against the Blazers. 
 This performance is obviously influenced by a lot of shot attempts and good efficiency from Precious. He won’t do this every game, but he will have the occasional game where he will score really well. If you want to use him as a streamer only, he could be worth taking a look at if you need some points and rebounds. Do not expect much more than that however. 
 Ben Simmons 
 SAC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #25 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Ben Simmons suffered a ruptured Achilles tendon during Sunday’s practice. 
 Simmons’ 2026-27 season reportedly ended in devastating fashion days before his official return to the NBA. The 6-foot-10 guard/forward signed with the Kings with the expectation that he would back up rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. However, Simmons showed enough during the preseason to earn a starting spot alongside Acuff. Sunday’s injury changes that, obviously, with Precious Achiuwa and De’Andre Hunter being potential replacements in the starting five. As for the point guard rotation, Malik Monk will be asked to take on more playmaking responsibilities off the bench. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa (ankle) recorded a double-double on Tuesday with 12 points (5-of-15 FGs), 11 rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in a 110-98 loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 The Kings just can’t keep a backup big healthy. Maxime Raynaud (knee) and Dylan Cardwell (calf) are both set to miss time, so Achiuwa got the start with Domantas Sabonis getting the night off. Achiuwa exited early with a right ankle injury after having a productive night. If he is also forced to miss the start of the season, Jonathan Mogbo would be next in line to back up Sabonis. 
 Dylan Cardwell 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #32 
 Dylan Cardwell is set to miss at least two weeks with a left calf strain. 
 After missing practice on Monday, Cardwell is now set to miss the start of the season. Maxime Raynaud (knee) has also been ruled out for the start of the season, so the Kings will be thin down low behind Domantas Sabonis. Precious Achiuwa will likely be tasked with filling the void in a limited capacity. 
 Ben Simmons 
 SAC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #25 
 Andscape’s Marc J. Spears reports that Ben Simmons is expected to remain in the starting lineup when the Kings open the regular season. 
 After sitting out the entire 2025-26 season, Simmons started and played nine minutes in his unofficial debut for the Kings on Saturday against the Warriors. At the time of his signing, reports said the veteran guard/forward was expected to back up rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr., but the Kings appear to have a different plan. Simmons, whose minutes will be increased in Sacramento’s final two preseason games, is expected to remain a starter. That likely pushes Precious Achiuwa to the bench, with Zach LaVine, Keegan Murray, and Domantas Sabonis rounding out the starting five. Despite Monday’s report, fantasy managers should still wait until the later rounds of drafts to select Simmons. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa amassed 18 points (9-of-13 FGs), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in Thursday’s exhibition against the Lakers. 
 After attempting just two shots in the Kings’ first meeting with the Lakers this preseason, Achiuwa was far more active on Thursday. Only Darius Acuff Jr. among the Kings’ starters took more shots, and Achiuwa shot well over 50 percent from the field. His viability as a fantasy option this season depends in part on Keegan Murray’s health, as he hasn’t played in either of Sacramento’s first two preseason games. While a healthy Murray would likely push De’Andre Hunter to the bench, his presence in the lineup could also mean fewer shots for Achiuwa. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Kings re-signed Precious Achiuwa to a two-year, $11.5 million contract, according to NBA Insider Chris Haynes. 
 Achiuwa had the best season of his young career last year as he averaged 10.1 points and 23.9 minutes in his first season with Sacramento. In the season’s final 25 games, he averaged 15.7 points and 9.2 rebounds in 31 minutes per game. Achiuwa stepped up when the Kings dealt with injuries to its frontline. He’s set to return as the backup power forward on a two-year deal. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa finished Wednesday’s win over the Raptors with 28 points (12-of-19 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 19 rebounds, one assist, one block and one three-pointer. 
 Achiuwa was outstanding on Wednesday, grabbing a season-high 19 rebounds and recording his 11th double-double of the season. By comparison, he recorded 12 double-doubles in his previous two seasons combined. The Kings’ frontcourt injuries have opened the door for Achiuwa, and on most nights, he’s taken advantage. Sacramento plays two more games in Week 23, starting with the Pelicans on Friday.

 Ty Jerome amassed 31 points (8-of-17 FGs, 14-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 For those who believed Jerome would cool off after scoring 73 points in the Grizzlies’ first two games, that didn’t happen on Sunday. He did most of his damage inside the arc, making 7 of 11 two-point attempts and shooting 14-for-14 from the foul line. Add in the assists, and it was another excellent night for those rostering Jerome, one of the best players in fantasy basketball so far. The Grizzlies play three games in Week 2, starting with the Jazz on Monday.

 Jaylen Brown accounted for 16 points (5-of-20 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Pistons.
 After a strong start in his first three appearances for the 76ers, Brown cooled off on Sunday. He shot 3-of-14 from inside the arc against the Pistons, and many of those misses came in the paint. There’s no need to lose any sleep over Brown’s performance against the Pistons, as the overall track record has been good. He’ll look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Pacers.

 LeBron James tallied 18 points (8-of-15 FGs, 2-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, five assists and two steals in Sunday’s loss to the Pistons.
 Back in the lineup after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Bucks, James played 33 minutes on Sunday. Some of those minutes came at center, as the 76ers did not have Joel Embiid. James had a decent night, but he wasn’t as impactful as many fantasy managers likely hoped in the 76ers’ final game of Week 1. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Tyrese Maxey 
 PHI

 #0 
 Player Stats

 Tyrese Maxey (head) finished Sunday’s loss to the Pistons with 29 points (11-of-24 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer.
 Maxey and the 76ers were playing their third game in four days. With LeBron James (Saturday) and Joel Embiid (Sunday) each missing a game, the 76ers’ star point guard had to shoulder a heavier workload. Despite that, Maxey still recorded an efficient stat line to end Week 1. There was an injury scare when he collided with Detroit’s John Collins in the fourth quarter, but Maxey was fine. Philadelphia plays three games in Week 2, starting with the Pacers on Wednesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 John Collins notched 16 points (7-of-15 FGs), 11 rebounds, two blocks and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the 76ers.
 Jalen Duren’s hamstring injury wouldn’t affect Collins’ place in the Pistons’ starting lineup. However, the All-Star center’s absence meant Collins would sometimes be the biggest Piston on the floor. Philadelphia didn’t have Joel Embiid on Sunday, which made the paint a bit more manageable for Detroit. But that shouldn’t take away from Collins’ double-double and blocked shots. Collins is already rostered in 80 percent of Yahoo leagues, and the Duren injury raises his fantasy ceiling. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Daniss Jenkins accumulated 18 points (6-of-11 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, one block and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the 76ers.
 Jenkins started Sunday’s game for the injured Ausar Thompson and, as he did on multiple occasions last season, gave the Pistons solid minutes in that role. Jenkins’ final stat line lacked only a steal, as he was impactful on both ends of the floor. Detroit begins Week 2 with a Tuesday/Wednesday back-to-back, making it possible Jenkins gets another start in one of those games (if not both, if Thompson remains out).

 Duncan Robinson recorded 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and five three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the 76ers.
 Robinson has started this season hot, scoring 17 points or more in each of Detroit’s first three games. Against the 76ers, he shot 5-of-9 from beyond the arc. Given his start to the season, Robinson is worth picking up while he’s rolling. He’s rostered in 33 percent of Yahoo leagues, so it won’t be too challenging to find Robinson on the waiver wire in 12-team leagues.

 Cade Cunningham finished Sunday’s win over the 76ers with 26 points (9-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), eight rebounds, eight assists, two steals, two blocks and three three-pointers.
 Cunningham and the Pistons remained undefeated after defeating the 76ers, doing so without two starters. With Jalen Duren out for at least two weeks and Ausar Thompson also unavailable on Sunday, Cunningham will have to do more of the heavy lifting for the Pistons in the short term. Beyond scoring, he provided excellent value for fantasy managers across the board. The Pistons play three games in Week 2, starting with the Knicks on Tuesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Josh Hart finished Sunday’s loss to the Magic with 13 points (5-of-12 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists, two steals and three three-pointers.
 While Mikal Bridges (six points, five rebounds, one assist, and one block) continues to offer limited fantasy value, Hart has started strong. The Knicks’ wing posted a strong stat line on Sunday and has been a top-50 fantasy player through the first week of the season. Expecting Hart to sustain that isn’t realistic, given all that he brings to the table. That said, some managers may consider selling high before Week 2.

 Jalen Brunson produced 28 points (12-of-28 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Magic.
 Brunson led all scorers with 28 points, but the Magic made him work for every shot that he took. The Knicks’ point guard needed 28 field-goal attempts to reach that total, and he made 1-of-7 from beyond the arc. As a team, New York shot 9-of-38 from three while Orlando was 18-of-42. Essentially, that was the ballgame. Brunson has been inefficient as a scorer so far, and things won’t get any easier for him when the Pistons visit MSG on Tuesday.
